newsitem.title: USA: BOXING-BOTHA SAYS MOORER HAS NO WAY TO STOP HIM.
newsitem.headline: BOXING-BOTHA SAYS MOORER HAS NO WAY TO STOP HIM.

text.p: Francois Botha makes no secret of why he feels he is going to beat Michael Moorer Saturday to regain the International Boxing Federation heavyweight crown.
"He's got no defence," Botha said of Moorer, whom he fights on the undercard of the Mike Tyson-Evander Holyfield World Boxing Association title fight at the MGM Grand.

Botha's bid to become the IBF champion a second time brings the year full circle for the 28-year-old South African, who began 1996 as the champion, after beating German Axel Schulz for the vacant title in December of last year.

But a few months later Botha was stripped of the crown for testing positive for steroids. Despite his penalty and having not fought at all this year, Botha was still named the Boxer of the Year by the IBF.
Moorer, 37-1, beat Schulz by decision for the vacant title on June 22 to begin his second reign as IBF champion and said he would remain champion because Botha is out of his league in this fight.
"By his record he looks like a formidable opponent," Moorer, a 5-1/2 to 1 favourite said Wednesday. "But he has not fought guys like I have."
"He is not on a level that I am," said Moorer of the 36-0 Botha.
Botha is confident after studying tapes of Moorer's only other title defence on November 5, 1994, when he was knocked out with one punch by George Foreman in the 10th round.
"He couldn't stay away from Foreman's punches and he is very slow," Botha said of the 47-year-old Foreman. "I know I'm faster and have power and speed. I know I'm going to connect."
Botha has stopped 21 opponents within the distance and figures to add another this week.
"If he trys to get up after I hit him the first time it would be a big mistake because I'll put him right back down," Botha said.
Moorer dismisses the tough talk as Botha's way of convincing himself that he can win.
"A lot of people try to hype themselves up, it doesn't mean anything to me," said Moorer. "He knows he can't beat me."
The stakes are huge for both fighters, as the winner will be the next likely foe to cash in on millions by taking on Tyson, if he beats Holyfield as expected.
Botha, however, suggested that the 29-year-old Moorer doesn't have the fortitude to stand up to either himself or Tyson.
"I really think the man doesn't want to fight," Botha said. "He doesn't want a piece of me and he wants nothing to do with Tyson."
